artworks.title: Danaë
artworks.description: Rembrandt's Hermitage Danaë waits in a shadowed bed as Zeus' golden light pours toward her — the Argive princess as intimate Baroque drama of desire and captivity. Oil on canvas, State Hermitage Museum, Saint Petersburg.

artworks.title: Danaë
artworks.description: Klimt curls Danaë into a gold-patterned coil as Zeus arrives as a shower of coin-like rain — the bronze tower myth restaged as Symbolist erotic ornament. Oil on canvas, Leopold Museum, Vienna.

artworks.title: Danaë
artworks.description: Artemisia paints Danaë and a servant receiving the golden rain — Zeus' visit as a charged exchange of light, flesh, and watchfulness. Oil on canvas, Saint Louis Art Museum.

artworks.title: Danaë
artworks.description: Correggio's Borghese Danaë reclines as Eros and putti manage the golden shower — soft High Renaissance flesh for the impregnation that will father Perseus. Oil on canvas, Galleria Borghese, Rome.

artworks.title: Danaë
artworks.description: Titian's Prado Danaë receives Zeus as a rain of gold while a maid gathers coins — the Argive confinement turned into Venetian sensual theatre. Oil on canvas, Museo del Prado, Madrid.

music.title: Die Liebe der Danae
music.description: Strauss's late mythological opera stages Zeus' golden rain and Danaë's choice between divine gold and mortal love — the Argive princess as a twentieth-century allegory of desire and wealth.

popCulture.title: Shower of gold
popCulture.description: English still names a sudden windfall a shower of gold — Zeus' visit to the bronze tower turned into a proverb for unexpected riches.
